title: Human Capital, Not Model Benchmarks, Predicts Hybrid Intelligence in Forecasting
abstract: Whether pairing people with AI helps or hurts is usually reported as a single average effect. Using a real-money prediction market (Polymarket) as an objective, externally resolved benchmark, this pilot shows that the value of human-AI collaboration depends on a specific, measurable form of human capital. Analyzed at the level of the individual forecaster, hybrid performance is trimodal: most people either deferred to the model (matching it) or used it to rubber-stamp a prior guess (performing worse than the model alone), while a minority engaged in genuine complementary reasoning and reached accuracy matching or even exceeding (i.e., lower error than) the market itself. Collaborative traits (perspective-taking, intellectual humility, and curiosity) rather than raw cognitive ability or model benchmarks, distinguished who reached that mode. The results are preliminary but statistically robust, and motivate a pre-registered replication now in preparation.

significance.justification: The paper identifies specific human traits that predict successful human-AI collaboration, providing actionable guidance for team composition and training in real-world AI deployment scenarios.

novelty.justification: While human-AI collaboration has been studied, the trimodal performance pattern and focus on collaborative traits rather than cognitive ability represents a substantial new variation in approach.

reproducibility.justification: The method uses a public prediction market (Polymarket) and describes the experimental design clearly enough for reimplementation, though no code or datasets are provided.

clarity.justification: The paper is well-written with clear claims, appropriate scope limitations noted as 'preliminary but statistically robust,' and a defensible evaluation methodology using real-money markets.

topical_fit.justification: Directly addresses human-AI collaboration dynamics, a core concern for builders implementing LLMs in real-world applications where human oversight and interaction are critical.
